note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute shortness of breath starting about 1 hour ago, while resting/sitting watching TV.
  - Postpartum status: had a cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
  - Cough began yesterday; no productive cough reported.
  - Baby is present with the patient.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - SOB began within the last hour; no chest pain reported; SOB described as increasing stress with noticeable palpitations.
  - Deep breaths associated with chest soreness (also tender from C-section scar).
- ENT symptoms:
  - No throat swelling/closing, no hoarseness, no odynophagia, no nasal/ocular symptoms described.
  - No dysphagia or drooling reported.
- Past medical history and treatments:
  - Recent C-section (4 weeks ago).
  - Regular use of Codeine for pain after C-section; current use not specified but mentioned as having taken it fairly regularly; last week not used.
  - Allergies: Ibuprofen allergy.
  - No other medical problems reported.
  - Prior episodes requiring ED care or injections not documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Ibuprofen allergy.
  - Codeine pain relief after C-section; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social context:
  - Accompanied by baby; partner at work; no other caregiver present.

Objective:
- Observable findings:
  - No ENT-specific swelling or airway edema described.
  - Respiratory status not formally quantified; patient reports SOB.
  - Heart rate self-assessed as fast; patient counted 30 beats during a brief self-check.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Shortness of breath reported; no stridor or obvious airway obstruction documented.
- Mental status:
  - Not described beyond reported anxiety about SOB.
- Vitals/exam findings:
  - Not formally recorded.
- Presence of others:
  - Baby is with patient; no other accompanying adult present (partner at work).

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Postpartum patient with acute shortness of breath after recent cesarean section; tachycardia suspected by patient and noted by clinician as slightly fast.
  - Clinician highlights risk of thromboembolic disease (including pulmonary embolism) given recent C-section and SOB; advised hospital evaluation.
  - No clear infectious or anaphylactic signs documented in the visit.
- Conflict noted:
  - None identified.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Advised to go to the hospital for evaluation; patient opted to self-transport rather than call an ambulance.
  - Do not take Codeine during this period.
  - Recommend bringing baby and essential items to the hospital.
- Specific instructions to patient/caregiver:
  - Go quickly to the hospital; ensure accompaniment or support as needed.
  - If any respiratory deterioration occurs (increased work of breathing, inability to speak full sentences, worsening chest pain, or new wheeze), seek emergency assistance.
  - Consider clinical evaluation for pulmonary embolism and post-surgical complications.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Breathing difficulty, voice change, throat closing, or worsening swelling should prompt urgent care or EMS.
- Follow-up:
  - Not specified in transcript; implication is evaluation in hospital for postpartum thromboembolism risk and further management.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions:
  - Noted that patient will go to hospital; no additional text from transcript to reproduce verbatim.
